headline: Blood bank and fridge attacks, Claude Dispatch hijack risk, Zyxel switch exploitation
overview: Today's shows lead with attacks on European blood bank and supermarket refrigeration systems, a Claude Dispatch flaw that could allow cross-boundary command execution, and a Zyxel switch zero-day used to compromise nearly a thousand devices. Several shows also flag fresh critical patches from Cisco, Barracuda, Chrome and Linux, plus Entra app-secret abuse and a Binance heist linked to North Korea.

topStories.title: Refrigeration and blood supply cyberattacks in Europe
topStories.summary: Hackers tampered with European refrigeration systems, disrupting blood banks and supermarket freezers. Several shows say the same attacks also hit a French blood plasma operator and a French bank heist estimated at about $133 million.

topStories.title: Zyxel switch zero-day exploited against nearly 1,000 devices
topStories.summary: Attackers exploited a Zyxel GS1900 switch flaw from August, stealing configurations and password hashes from roughly a thousand devices. A second flaw reportedly works even on switches patched in June, and many looted devices still had factory passwords.

topStories.title: Claude Dispatch flaw and AI-era security concerns
topStories.summary: Anthropic reportedly declined to fix a Claude Dispatch flaw that could let attackers run remote commands across corporate boundaries. Other AI-related items include OpenAI facing questions over past security warnings and attempts to prove which AI model produced an answer.

topStories.title: Critical patches and unpatched Linux and firewall flaws
topStories.summary: Cisco and WatchGuard shipped critical patches while SonicWall will not fix flaws in its end-of-life GMS product. A Debian and Ubuntu APT signature bypass lets attackers inject packages, and a Linux TCP kernel flaw allows remote root on some systems, with Ubuntu's fix still pending.

topStories.title: Entra app secret abuse and supply-chain tampering
topStories.summary: Attackers used stolen app secrets to sign into trusted Entra apps through MSPs, reaching at least 27 organisations. A fake update to CPGuard reached nearly 3,000 Linux hosting servers after a trial-account compromise of the vendor's billing portal.

topStories.title: Binance heist and North Korea attribution
topStories.summary: Binance detailed a multi-billion-dollar theft attributed to North Korea, and one show notes that fake job interviews helped enable the theft. Separately, a Canadian faced charges for hacking U.S. universities.

episodes.title: Claude, you've got company.
episodes.summary: Covers the Claude Dispatch flaw, residential proxies on White House networks, Asian airline breaches tied to Amadeus, Cisco and WatchGuard patches, GhostMap Android reboot loops, the Zyxel zero-day, and a Ukrainian scam crackdown. Also includes a guest interview on the NIST post-quantum roadmap.

episodes.title: Ballots, bots, and backlash.
episodes.summary: Covers election-day technical glitches and misinformation, hacks on European refrigeration systems, OpenAI security-warning scrutiny, Nvidia restrictions on Chinese customers, the Binance heist, Barracuda patches, and Canadians charged for hacking U.S. universities. Includes an industry interview with Box's CISO on enterprise AI security.

episodes.title: Blood bank fridge hacks, Anthropic model identity, Google Calendar phishing
episodes.summary: Covers blood bank fridge attacks in Europe, Anthropic's work on proving which AI model answered, Google Calendar phishing that hijacks sessions, a Chinese keyboard app used to deliver malware, a French bank heist of about $133 million, and an APT29-linked campaign against unpatched phones.

episodes.title: SANS Stormcast Thursday, November 5th, 2026: Email Test Scripts; runZero oobscan BMC/IPMI; apt Signature Bypass (CVE-2026-109518); SonicWall GMS EOL Unpatched Flaws
episodes.summary: Covers attempts to find exposed test email scripts that can leak configuration and send spam, a new out-of-band management scanner from runZero, a critical APT signature bypass, and SonicWall GMS flaws that will not be fixed as the product is end of life.

episodes.title: Why a Data Center Slowdown Benefits Big Tech
episodes.summary: Discusses how a slowdown in data center construction could benefit large tech firms, alongside headlines on ChatGPT search, a Meta acquisition, and Apple AI spending limits. Other episodes in the feed cover AI self-improvement and benchmark rankings; this is general AI industry news rather than security.

episodes.title: How the Midterm Results Change AI
episodes.summary: Looks at how the midterm election results could affect data center construction, AI regulation, and the 2028 presidential race, with the backlash possibly leading to better local community deals rather than a halt to AI build-out. This is AI policy rather than security news.

episodes.title: That's Not Supposed to Happen - PSW #951
episodes.summary: Covers supermarket refrigeration attacks, a Linux TCP kernel flaw, the Binance theft, a Google Android TV botnet takedown, AI-assisted exploit development, emergency alert app hijacking, and a railway employee blaming an intrusion on AI. The notes are a topic list with little detail on each.

episodes.title: Zyxel 2nd Switch 0-Day, 1K Hacked, Debian/Ubuntu APT MitM Flaw, France Blood Supply Cyberattack
episodes.summary: Covers a second Zyxel switch zero-day that compromised about a thousand devices, a Debian and Ubuntu APT man-in-the-middle flaw, and a cyberattack on the French blood supply. Also mentions AI-linked breaches at several firms and a Chrome 157 release with 213 fixes.

episodes.title: APT29-linked phone exploits, Zyxel patch bypass, White House proxy | Cyber Security News Nov 5
episodes.summary: Covers APT29-linked exploitation of out-of-date phones through hacked websites, the Zyxel switch flaw and password theft, a DreamHost file manager login compromise, Debian and Ubuntu APT tampering, Xen hypervisor memory flaws, Cisco Snort 3 and Foglight issues, SonicWall GMS, a DigiCert system exposure, and residential proxy use from the White House network.

episodes.title: Hospital Diverts Ambulances, 5.7M Breached by a Phone Call, Town Pays $82K Ransom
episodes.summary: Covers ransomware forcing a New Mexico Level 1 trauma center to divert ambulances, a new group claiming access to many systems, and a phone-based social engineering breach affecting about 5.7 million people at Marathon Health. Aimed at business leaders, with a focus on recovery planning.

episodes.title: How AI agents are spooking the banks
episodes.summary: Discusses AI agents calling banks on users' behalf, a Florida man indicted over a ransomware recovery fraud, and fake job interviews linked to Binance losses. The episode page mentions sponsored content and an interview with Dropzone AI on AI-driven alert triage; the rest is mostly show banter.

episodes.title: ARTEX for Everyone: What Widely Available AI Hacking Means for Defenders
episodes.summary: Discusses ARTEX, an openly available AI-powered penetration-testing framework now appearing in real intrusions, and what defenders can do, such as rotating exposed credentials and using AI-enabled red-team tools. This is a vendor-hosted discussion, so it is sponsored.

episodes.title: Stolen Entra app secrets, cPGuard update hijack, Binance fake interview | Cyber Security News Nov 4
episodes.summary: Covers attackers abusing stolen Entra app secrets through MSPs, the CPGuard update hijack, exploitation of a Node-RED editor flaw, WS_FTP admin credential exposure, Barracuda email gateway patches, a Linux kernel flaw, Zyxel GS1900 firmware, Chrome 157 fixes, an Android update, and a forged GitHub commit.

episodes.title: 🎙️ Linux Kernel TCP Use-After-Free Gives Remote Unauthenticated Root on Every Major Distribution, Barracuda Critical Flaws Allow Root Access to Security Appliances, Google Dismantles 1.3 Million Devi
episodes.summary: Covers a Linux TCP use-after-free flaw giving remote root on major distributions, Barracuda root-access flaws in security appliances, Google's takedown of a 1.3 million device Android botnet, Android's November patches, European supermarket refrigeration disruption, and a password manager security incident.
